title: Pulse Beam Funnel Citadel — Six-Hour Witness Blueprint
page0: Treat the Funnel Hall as a real place. Imagine a meticulous observer physically occupying it for six hours and continuously describing every visible, audible, spatial, material, architectural, interactive, atmospheric and functional detail until there are no hand-waved surfaces left. Use that observation to ask the best open-ended design questions, run those questions through the Funnel, produce an end-to-end blueprint, then build the blueprint into Pulse without replacing live Funnel data with decorative fiction.
correctedQuestion: If the Pulse Beam Funnel Citadel had to withstand six hours of close physical observation as a convincing, beautiful, explorable civic-scale place—not a WebGL demo—what complete architecture, material system, lighting system, holographic language, traversal, utility, ambient behavior and performance strategy would make every direction and distance feel intentionally designed while the live Funnel graph remains the factual heart of the room?
questionBlueprint: What would a patient observer notice in the first ten seconds, after ten minutes, after an hour, and after six hours that distinguishes a designed place from a decorated visualization?
Where does the eye land from every major approach, balcony, threshold, stair, lounge and control position, and what secondary discoveries reward turning around?
Which surfaces need real geometry, thickness, seams, reveals, supports, fasteners, recesses or material transitions so the building reads as constructed rather than spawned?
How can the live Funnel graph become luminous architectural infrastructure without turning nodes into generic balls or glass ornaments?
What should physically emit, catch, occlude and reflect the holographic light so the laser system appears to inhabit the room?
How should active, candidate, verified, dormant and ordinary graph relationships differ without inventing state that does not exist?
How can the map-like glass UI language migrate into consoles, rails, wayfinding, observation glass and inspection surfaces without becoming a wall of HUD panels?
What spaces exist because a real visitor would use them: arrival, orientation, observation, circulation, inspection, quiet study, system control and return path?
What architectural rhythm keeps a large dark room legible on a phone screen while still rewarding desktop-scale exploration?
Which details can be procedural and deterministic so the room feels rich without requiring a giant authored asset payload?
What should move slowly, what should pulse only when live data justifies it, and what should remain completely still so motion retains meaning?
How should audio, fog, additive light, reflections and exposure be restrained so quality comes from contrast and proportion rather than effects spam?
What is the graceful low-power/mobile version of every expensive feature rather than simply deleting half the room?
What must remain selectable, traceable and connected to Foundry/Refinery so the monument is operational infrastructure rather than sculpture?
What tests prove that the six-hour design intent survived implementation?

witness.role: A patient architectural observer with no implementation knowledge. He reports what exists, not how it was coded.
witness.observation:
I enter through a compressed dark threshold and the room opens upward instead of merely outward. The first thing I notice is not a menu but a vertical field of cold light suspended over a black circular datum in the floor. The light has structure: razor-thin rings, converging laser ribs, vertical registration lines and moving packets that make relationships readable before I know their names. Nothing looks like a glass ball pretending to be important. The funnels are drawn in light like precise optical instruments. Their rims are brighter than their bodies; six or eight disciplined rays converge to a focus; faint contour rings let my eye complete the volume without filling it with plastic geometry. The largest live structure occupies the center while specialist structures hang at distinct elevations and distances.

The floor is nearly black polished stone broken into radial slabs with hairline metal inlays. Only selected registration axes catch ice-blue light. Around the central instrument is a shallow recessed projection well with a raised metal lip, a second ring of darker stone, calibration ticks and narrow service seams. Reflections are controlled rather than mirror-perfect: elongated traces of the lasers appear below me, but the floor remains stone.

Above, concentric structural rings hang from dark radial trusses. Some carry optical projectors; others tiny white service lights. The center is a deep layered machine crown rather than a flat ceiling decoration, and one vertical datum beam connects ceiling, graph and floor. It brightens at intersections and nearly disappears between them, making the room feel calibrated.

The perimeter is a building, not a boundary. Tall structural ribs divide smoked-glass wall bays. Behind some are dim service cavities, behind others distant light wells, and several reveal planted lounges. Columns have bases, shadow gaps and luminous service strips recessed into one face. No giant glowing rectangles are pasted onto walls.

A mezzanine wraps the room but breaks at the entrance and view corridors. Its underside is ribbed and dark. Its outer edge has a thin glass guard with a metal cap that becomes visible when lasers cross behind it. Two broad stair flights rise from the main floor. Each tread carries a tiny warm-neutral edge light, deliberately warmer than the hologram so circulation separates from information. The stairs land at observation level where the graph can be read in plan.

The consoles are physical plinths with sloped smoked-glass surfaces and a few map-like lines floating close to the glass. Information is absent until I approach or select something. The UI looks optically laminated into the surface: dark glass, thin white geometry, ice-blue selection, emerald only for verified or live state.

After an hour I notice quieter systems. Ceiling tracks carry tiny inspection drones on slow deterministic paths. Floor locator lights mark circulation but stop near the central instrument. Planters are concentrated in sheltered lounge pockets rather than scattered as decoration. Their leaves are dark enough to disappear until they catch reflected ice light. Benches have real bases and sit where the graph can be observed without blocking movement.

The lasers never become a screensaver. Edge flows move only along real graph relationships. Active authority is emerald and crisp. Candidate law is bright neutral white with restrained modulation. Ordinary relationships are dimmer ice and cyan. A selected path gains intensity while unrelated paths recede. Packets travel at deterministic phases, so the network feels alive without twitching.

At close range every funnel has a bright rim, descending contour rings, converging side rays, a central datum line and a tiny lower focus point. There is no opaque cone. Larger funnels gain additional optical structure instead of thicker plastic. Graph connections are narrow luminous tubes with bright cores and softer halos; their curves bend gently upward between endpoints, giving the network clearance and depth.

Hours later the architecture still has discoveries because detail is hierarchical. Wall bays alternate glass, ribbed metal, recessed shadow and controlled openings. The mezzanine has seams. The projection well has calibration marks. Rail posts occur at believable intervals. Ceiling rings have projector pods. Lounges have low furniture and planting. The threshold has a compressed canopy. Proportion, geometry, roughness, transmission and light communicate construction without a giant texture payload.

From above, the central floor reads like a map: concentric circles, radial axes and the live network floating above. From ground level it reads like a cathedral-scale instrument. From the threshold it is a destination. From the lounges it is infrastructure to study. Turning around always reveals a clear exit. The building never traps me in spectacle.

The sound is barely there: a low electrical and air-handling fundamental plus a quiet upper harmonic, no melody. It is opt-in. Reduced-motion or muted preference leaves the room respectable in silence.

Six hours later the room still makes sense because the beauty is not a pile of effects. The building has structural order, the hologram has information order, the UI has interaction order, and the live Funnel graph supplies the truth. The architecture amplifies that truth instead of impersonating it.

answer.name: Funnel Citadel / Optical Civic Instrument
answer.thesis: Build a complete radial civic interior around a factual live graph. Use constructed architectural geometry for the building and additive optical geometry for the Funnel network. Eliminate sphere-node aesthetics. Make the hologram read through rings, rays, tubes, focus points, projection hardware and controlled reflections. Detail the entire 360-degree envelope with hierarchy rather than noise.

constructionLanguage: structural ribs with bases and shadow gaps
layered ceiling trusses and optical rings
mezzanine with underside ribs and glass guard
physical console plinths with laminated glass UI
projection well lip, calibration ticks and service seams

materials.floor: near-black polished stone; moderate roughness and clearcoat, never perfect mirror
materials.glass: smoked optical glass with restrained transmission

hologram.rule: No visible sphere nodes and no opaque/glass cone bodies.
hologram.funnelGlyph: Nested elliptical laser rims + converging side rays + central datum + lower focus point. Scale/detail communicates hierarchy.
hologram.lawGlyph: Architectural optical sigil made from crossing axes and orbital rings; active emerald, candidate white.
hologram.edges: Curved luminous tubes with bright core, soft halo and deterministic moving packets. Selection raises intensity; unrelated edges recede.
hologram.projection: Ceiling projector crown + floor projection well visually explain where light originates.
hologram.truth: Every visible node/edge comes from FUNNEL_ENVIRONMENT_GRAPH; missing live data produces an explicit unavailable state.

interaction.movement: drag/touch look, WASD and mobile movement pad; observation-level toggle retained
interaction.inspection: invisible hit geometry surrounds optical glyphs; selecting opens factual node label/detail/state
interaction.navigation: Foundry and Refinery remain one action away; right-edge return to Create remains available
interaction.progressiveUI: normal view stays sparse; detail appears on selection/approach rather than permanent dashboard chrome

performance.mobile: lower pixel ratio, fewer contour rings, fewer rail posts/projectors/packets, simplified shadows and no decorative drones where necessary
performance.desktop: denser architecture and optical layers, still deterministic
performance.rule: Degrade density, not design language. The same room composition survives every tier.

preserve: v44 ACTIVE vs Ultra CANDIDATE semantics

acceptance: Funnel run reaches EXECUTION_AUTHORIZED and mints verified BlueprintReceipt and ExecutionReceipt.
No visible sphere geometry represents Funnel nodes.
Funnel glyphs are optical line/ray structures with multiple contour levels and a focus point.
Live graph edges are rendered as curved luminous relationships with deterministic flow packets.
The room contains a complete floor, ceiling, perimeter, mezzanine, circulation, consoles, lounge/planting and projection hardware rather than a central object in an empty shell.
At least five architectural detail systems are procedurally repeated with deterministic spacing.
Active law remains emerald and candidate law remains white/neutral.
Mobile receives the same spatial composition at reduced density.
Foundry, Refinery, inspection, observation level and Create return remain functional.
Pulse Beam existing checks remain valid.
